Messages.Author: Mark Lamutt
Messages.Body:
1. Can multiple Torn Signposts be played at the beginning of the same
round of combat to increase base strength, or can only 1 be played?

2. Bianca (at least I think she's the one) has a base of 2 hand damage
according to the jyhad text. Can torn signpost be played with her to
reset her strength to 3 (+1 from the TS and +1 from her)?

Thanks,
Mark

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Mark Wrote:
"1. Can multiple Torn Signposts be played at the beginning of the same
round of combat to increase base strength, or can only 1 be played?"

Well, as Torn Signpost sets your hand damage to 2 (or 3 at superior), you can
play as many as you want at the begining of combat, but as each one will just
set your hand damage to 2(or 3), it won't really do anything other than let you
cycle cards. So yes, you can play as many as you want, but you will still only
get the effect (2 or 3 hand damage) once due to the card text. The card you
are looking for is Fists of Death with gives you +1 (or +2) hand damage for the
entire combat, and as such, is completely stackable. You can play TS for 2
hand damage, and then play, say, 3 Fists of Death (each for +1 hand damage) to
get 5 hand damage, and then strike with Undead Strength for a total of 6 hand
damage (which would be 11 hand damage if you had superior Potence...)

"2. Bianca (at least I think she's the one) has a base of 2 hand damage
according to the jyhad text. Can torn signpost be played with her to
reset her strength to 3 (+1 from the TS and +1 from her)?"

Officially, yes, as now all vampires that used to have 2 hand damage (Bianca,
Zack North, etc) now have "+1 hand damage" instead. If this were not the case,
and then actually had 2 hand damage (instead of "+1"), then inferior Torn
Signpost would have no effect (but superior woudl still give them 3 hand
damage). Luckily, this is moot, as these vampires are all errattaed to have
"+1 hand damage" now (due to this being the change in the VTES reprint).

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
Mark Lamutt wrote:
>
> 1. Can multiple Torn Signposts be played at the beginning of the same
> round of combat to increase base strength, or can only 1 be played?
>

Play as many as you want. Each one will set your hand damage to 2/3.
Playing 15 Torn Signposts, all at superior, will net you a base hand
damage of 3. Playing 60 Torn Signposts, all at superior, will also net
you a base hand damage of 3.

> 2. Bianca (at least I think she's the one) has a base of 2 hand damage
> according to the jyhad text. Can torn signpost be played with her to
> reset her strength to 3 (+1 from the TS and +1 from her)?
>

All vampires that say "2 hand damage" actually have +1 hand damage (most
recent printing). Therefore, an inferior TS will give her 2 base hand
damage, and her text gives her an extra +1, for a total of 3.

-Chris

>> round of combat to increase base strength, or can only 1 be played?"

As I've read the rules, you could NOT play 3 Fists of Death or multiples of
ANY cards in the same combat or as Action Modifier cards. You could not
play three Faceless Nights on a single action, for instance.

The Wizard Marex

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:

You've read the rules wrong. That rule applies only to action modifiers
and reactions. The only other similar limits are a) No Repeat Actions,
and b) cards which grant additional strikes (only one additional strike
granting effect may be used each round... may be overridden by card
text).

-Chris

Messages.Author: Jasper Phillips
Messages.Body:
In article <73cs41$1...@news.millennianet.com>, Gabriel <j...@rfd.com> wrote:
>>> Mark Wrote:
>>> "1. Can multiple Torn Signposts be played at the beginning of the same
>>> round of combat to increase base strength, or can only 1 be played?"
>
>As I've read the rules, you could NOT play 3 Fists of Death or multiples of
>ANY cards in the same combat or as Action Modifier cards. You could not
>play three Faceless Nights on a single action, for instance.

Well, you're wrong.

True, you may not play multiple copies of the same action modifier or
reaction during a given action.

However, combat is not an action, and is in no way restricted by this
(certain cards with specific text otherwise excepted).
